Subject: Hosted API commit inquiry / volume discounts

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency and cost profile looked promising. Procurement asked me to follow up on annual commit options for our hosted API usage. We're planning an initial production rollout in Q4 and want clarity on:

- Typical starter vs. growth vs. enterprise token commit bands (tokens/month and annual minimums)
- Corresponding per-token price at each tier and how discounts step with volume
- Flex-credit mechanics (unused tokens credit, rolling vs. non-rolling)
- Ramp/overage treatment and any cap on effective unit price

Can you share a concise tiered proposal we can present to the procurement committee? We're on a mildly accelerated cadence and would like to get commit options and an SOW by early next week if possible.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of CloudOps
CloudPilot Inc.

Hi Sarah — appreciated the product session.

Quick summary attached: a compact portfolio with three annual commit paths (Starter, Growth, Enterprise) plus an optional flex-credit add-on. High-level bullets below; the workbook (Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v1.xlsx) has line-item math and sample token curves based on the usage snapshot you sent.

Starter — 500M tokens / year (≈41.7M tokens/mo)
- Base per-token: $0.00045
- Discount: 5% off list for 12-month commitment
- Flex credits optional at +$5k/year (allows 10% unused to roll as credits)

Growth — 2.5B tokens / year (≈208M tokens/mo)
- Base per-token: $0.00035
- Discount: 12% off list; additional 3% for 24-month term
- Included burst pool to handle 20% occasional spikes without overage billing (subject to fair use)

Enterprise — 10B tokens / year (≈833M tokens/mo)
- Base per-token: $0.00022
- Negotiated tiered rebates tied to attainment (up to an additional 6%)
- Optional private VPC deployment add-on and extended retention SLA

Overage and ramp
- Overage billed at list price with the first 10% overage discounted by the negotiated tier rate for the first month of ramp.
- We can build a staged ramp schedule into the SOW to smooth billing and credits.

Flex-credit model (brief)
- Add-on for Starter/Growth: small fixed fee that allows a fraction of unused committed tokens to convert to off-invoice credits usable within 12 months.
- Enterprise flex terms are fully negotiable and can include carry-forward and quota reallocation across product lines.

Next steps
- I'm attaching the workbook and a SOW stub. If this looks directionally right, can we schedule a 30-minute procurement call Tues 8/31 to lock terms and hand to legal?

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vivek — quick notes from pricing ops:

Thanks for drafting. A couple of tactical tweaks before we present:

- Starter: make the flex-credit opt-in fee $4k (help it land cheaper for SMBs).
- Growth: change burst pool wording to "burst buffer" and limit to 15% unless they buy burst add-on.
- Enterprise: propose an attainment rebate schedule at 2% per quarter over 90% attainment, capped at 6%.

Karthik, can you confirm marginal economics for the Growth breakpoint at 2.5B? We need to ensure the unit economics don't slip below our floor when factoring in burst credit usage.

Also, legal will want the carry-forward language for flex credits to be explicit in the SOW. I'll loop in legal once Sarah gives a green light to proceed.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-28T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit inquiry / volume discounts

On Thu, Aug 27, 2026 at 11:18 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik, can you confirm marginal economics for the Growth breakpoint at 2.5B? We need to ensure the unit economics don't slip below our floor when factoring in burst credit usage.

Checked the model. Short answer: safe with current assumptions but depends on two levers:

1) Effective utilization of cached tokens (we assumed 12% prefix reuse for CloudPilot's profile). If cache reuse drops under 6%, the floor tightens by ~8%.
2) Burst buffer realization — if they exercise the full 15% buffer consistently, incremental cost could exceed the discounted rate for the first 90 days. Recommend adding a phased buffer (10% first quarter, 15% thereafter) in the SOW.

Updated suggestion for the customer-facing doc:
- Growth base: $0.00036 per token (move up $0.00001 to protect floor)
- Keep 12% discount, 24-month further 3% as discussed
- Flex-credit opt-in fee $4k for Starter/Growth

I'll attach a one-tab sensitivity snapshot to the workbook before you send.

Karthik Iyer
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
